note: Inputs for the "What's exposed" panel (docs/design/mitigations.md; Eric's decisions E6-E8). Sites point at data/sites-checked.json by id, or at a mapped place in data/facilities.json by label. 'kind' is what a flood could carry off: 'in use' (materials stored or handled now) or 'in ground' (contamination in soil or groundwater). 'verified' is true where the description was checked against the State record (C18); false would mark a research agent's reading not yet re-read. Business and public facility names only.

sites.name: City transfer station and recycling center, Second St at Gilman St
sites.holds: Garbage, recycling and compost in transfer; a hazardous materials locker for illegally disposed hazardous materials pulled from the tipping floor; cathode ray tubes, fluorescent bulbs and batteries; a 1,000-gallon double-walled used oil tank (transfer station Draft EIR, PDF pp. 81-83). Its runoff carried metals, acid, oil and grease above state limits before a 2016 settlement (F14).
sites.costs: Doing nothing here carries a rebuild need of $120 million in the City's proposed 2027-31 capital plan, unfunded beyond $1.85 million, with no bond yet; the Zero Waste Fund's net position was −$0.9 million in FY2025. The station's own operating cost is not published; it takes in about $10 million a year. No study of closing it or using a regional station was found; a 2015 study of franchising commercial service modeled $4 million a year in fees, 25 jobs lost, and $2.2 million a year of overhead moved onto residential and station customers, which the new fees would cover (Z1-Z4).

sites.name: Former Pacific Steel Casting, Second St (closed 2018)
sites.holds: Contaminated soil and groundwater; groundwater as shallow as 1.5 ft below ground, with petroleum free product in places; possible PCBs in the plant's concrete (Gilman Gateway Final EIR, F17). Cleanup open; DTSC voluntary agreement active (F19).

sites.name: Berkeley Forge & Tool, 1331 Eastshore Hwy
sites.holds: An active industrial site under the state's industrial stormwater permit as of October 2024 (Gilman Gateway Draft EIR, F18); runoff with aluminum, copper, iron and zinc before a 2012 settlement (F16). Listed among the City's high-risk hazardous materials facilities (T2).

sites.name: 1255 Eastshore Hwy (former Hawkins Traffic Safety Supply)
sites.holds: Chlorinated solvents (TCE, DCE, vinyl chloride) and gasoline-range hydrocarbons in soil, shallow groundwater and soil vapor, in fill under a former traffic-sign plant; the Water Board believes the solvents detected in 2019 come from off the site. Case open, eligible for closure since April 2022 (GeoTracker T10000011080).

sites.name: Berkeley Marine Center boatyard, 1 Spinnaker Way
sites.holds: A boatyard; lead and copper in surface and near-surface soil, found by 2008 after a City Parks complaint and on the waterfront in 2009; stormwater collection and filtering were added. Case open, in site assessment since July 2020 (GeoTracker T10000001877). Whether the boatyard operates now is not in the case record.

sites.name: Terminal Manufacturing, 707 Gilman St
sites.holds: PCE, diesel and gasoline in groundwater and soil vapor, found in 2016 during tank investigations; groundwater treatment injections began by 2020. Case open, in verification monitoring since July 2023 (GeoTracker T10000009006). Whether the plant operates now is not in the case record.

sites.name: Eastshore State Park shoreline parcels
sites.holds: PCBs, lead and other metals in soil and groundwater. The 1998 cleanup dug out 4,600 cubic yards of shallow soil at 17 locations across the park; Water Board Order 98-072 requires ongoing risk management, including shoreline erosion control, with annual inspections. Case open, long-term management (GeoTracker SL0600164054, which covers the park in Berkeley, Albany and Richmond).

sites.name: Former Flint Ink, 750 Gilman St
sites.holds: A black ink plant from 1900 to 2004. Lead, kerosene and other petroleum; volatile organic compounds remain in groundwater in the northeast corner. The 2005-06 cleanup removed 19,000 tons of soil and about 370,000 gallons of groundwater; two possibly leaking tanks were closed in place under slabs of historic buildings. Case open, eligible for closure since October 2021 (GeoTracker SL0600172262).

sites.name: Former Berkeley Landfill under César Chávez Park
sites.holds: About 1.5 million tons of residential, commercial and industrial waste, placed from 1961 to 1983 directly on Bay Mud with no engineered base liner, inside perimeter levees built 1957-1968 and armored with riprap in the late 1970s (Water Board tentative order, February 2010, p. 2). Water Board staff reported investigations showing the leachate is not in hydraulic connection to the Bay (staff summary, April 14, 2010). A still-water level does not describe its hazard: waves and Bay water on its edges, groundwater in the waste.

marinaRoutesNote: University Ave counts only west of grid x = 2300 m (I-80), as the City study's raised-road preset does (data/plans.json).

gaps.title: Transfer station: tsunami release judged only against today
gaps.text: Its Draft EIR places the site in the tsunami hazard area but finds no risk of releasing pollutants, because rebuilding would not make the site more exposed than it is now. It requires nothing. Its search for another site tested size, zoning and availability, not flood, sea level rise or tsunami exposure.

gaps.title: Gilman Gateway: design floor from superseded guidance
gaps.text: The project's minimum floor for critical infrastructure is 13.4 ft NAVD88: the nearby flood elevation plus 3.4 ft of rise from the 2018 State guidance. Today's 100-year storm tide plus the 2024 guidance's rise at the San Francisco gauge gives 14.53 (Intermediate-High) and 16.23 (High) ft NAVD88 of still water in 2100, figures this explorer derives (C13). Its tsunami-proof storage rule (HYD-4) covers only future development on that site.

gaps.title: City hazard mitigation plan: pollutants named, sites not
gaps.text: One sentence says tsunamis can release hazardous materials; no facility is named. Its two tsunami actions are low priority and concern Marina docks.

gaps.title: The 2024 tsunami warning review: people, not sites
gaps.text: The City cleared the Marina in 45 minutes. Its after-action report and twelve recommendations never mention hazardous materials, industry or the transfer station.

gaps.title: State hazardous materials rules: earthquake, not flood or tsunami
gaps.text: Business plans must cover a release and consider earthquakes; no requirement to plan for flood or tsunami was found. The State's tsunami map has no regulatory force for the sites inside it.

gaps.title: The landfill's Water Board order: no tsunami
gaps.text: It covers the 100-year flood and erosion of waste; it does not mention tsunami. A draft 2026 order adds 2050 sea level rise and wave run-up, still without tsunami.

gaps.title: The City's contaminated-site screening: daily high tide only
gaps.text: It checks 427 sites against rising groundwater and the average daily high tide. It does not consider storm tides, Bay water up the storm drains, or trapped rain, which this explorer shows.

gaps.title: Storm drain outfalls: tide gates not published
gaps.text: Which outfalls have working tide gates is not public, and it decides whether the Bay comes up through the drains at the sites above.
